section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection between "redeem my soul in peace" and the stone becoming one, paralleling how Israel makes the aspect of "one" manifest even in worldly matters.
section.t: And based on this, the connection of "Redeem my soul in peace" to what is said "And this stone etc." is also understood,
for this, that from "the stones of the place" (plural) it became "one stone," is like the matter of "with many were they with me."
And in this manner is also the matter of "You are One etc." and "Who is like Your people Israel, one nation in the land,"
for the novelty of "one nation in the land" is as the Alter Rebbe explained,
that Israel draws down the aspect of "one" even into matters of the land.
For even though matters of the land are in the aspect of plurality,
and even in the creation of Adam, our sages of blessed memory said,
on the verse,
"Let us make"
(in the plural),
"man,"
"What, do you give an opening for heretics etc.?" and "whoever wishes to err etc.,"
meaning that this is such a concealment that even Moshe Rabbeinu, the wisdom of holiness, said "What, do you give etc.,"
behold, even within this aspect of plurality, the aspect of "one" is made.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the discourse of the Baal HaHilula on "Atem Nitzavim," questioning why the verse lists ten categories of Israel in two separate verses and why it specifies "your stranger who is within your camp."
section.t: D)
And all this will be understood by prefacing the discourse
(found in a book recently redeemed from captivity)
of the Baal HaHilula, beginning with the words "Atem Nitzavim,"
which explains
there that the enumeration of the types within Israel is divided into two levels
(as will be explained below).
And as an introduction,
that first it is stated in the verse,
"Your heads, your tribes etc., every man of Israel,"
and afterwards it is stated in a separate verse,
"Your little ones, your wives etc.,"
and the division of the verses also indicates a division of the subjects,
and superficially it needs to be understood,
why does it divide them into two separate verses?
Also, it needs to be understood,
since it says "You are standing today, all of you,"
why does it enumerate all ten levels and types within Israel,
and not suffice with what is said "all of you"?
Also, there needs to be explanation regarding what is said "and your stranger who is within your camp,"
why does it add specifically regarding the stranger that he is "within your camp"?

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the ten types of Israel correspond to the ten Sefiros of Atzilus, divided into two general levels of gadlus and katnus, detailing each category from "your heads" to "every man of Israel."
section.t: E)
And it explains there,
that the ten types within Israel correspond to the ten Sefiros of Atzilus,
and therefore they are divided into two general levels,
just as in the Sefiros there are two general levels,
the first Sefiros which are in the aspect of gadlus (greatness),
and the last Sefiros which are in the aspect of katnus (smallness).
And it should be added,
that based on this it can be explained that the first level in the first division is "your heads,"
and the first level in the second division is "your little ones,"
for,
the first level in each division indicates the totality of all the aspects within that division
(similar to the first letter of a word which includes all the letters of the word,
as explained in Shaar HaYichud VeHaEmunah),
and behold, "your heads" is the totality of the matter of gadlus,
and "your little ones" is the totality of the matter of katnus
(as will be explained below).
And it explains there,
that "your heads" is the aspect of Keter of Keter,
which includes all the particular heads,
and it is the aspect of the simple and essential will of the Congregation of Israel in general and of every Elokis spark in particular,
for which there is no reason at all for the will,
not even a hidden reason etc.,
as at the Giving of the Torah, as it is written,
"And Israel encamped there etc."
[And it should be added,
that also the matter of drawing down the aspect of the supernal will within all of Israel,
is understood based on what is said at the Giving of the Torah, "I am Havayah your God,"
as explained in many places,
that then the aspect of "I am Havayah" became the power and vitality of each and every one of Israel].
And afterwards it said "your tribes,"
which are called "the tribes of Yah,"
as it is written,
"For there the tribes ascended, the tribes of Yah,"
and it is the aspect of the light of Keter that spreads into Chochmah and Binah within Keter itself, and is called Chochmah and Binah of Keter etc.,
and it is the revelation of the essential will that illuminates within the concealment of the intellect, which is called a hidden reason for the will.
[And it is noteworthy,
that what is explained here is unlike what is explained elsewhere,
that what is written "For there the tribes ascended, the tribes of Yah" refers to Chochmah and Binah as they are in their place].
And afterwards it said "your elders,"
"elder" who has acquired wisdom,
from its source, to bring it from concealment etc. to come into expansion in Binah,
and these are the Sanhedrin, who are the judges and magistrates etc.
And afterwards it said "your officers,"
which is the aspect of Netzach and Hod of Chochmah and Binah
(this is the matter of the kidneys
that advise),
which are the strength and power of the light of intellect for the brain to rule over the heart
etc.,
and they are like the agents of the judges who coerce the people with a rod to subdue them so they do not deviate from the judgment of the Torah to the right or left,
as it is written,
"Judges and officers etc."
And afterwards it said "every man of Israel,"
which is the aspect of Daas that spreads into the emotions, which is divided into 600,000 opinions,
as is known regarding the blessing of "Chacham HaRazim" over 600,000 of Israel whose opinions are not similar one to another,
and even until Daas spreads into the emotions of Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferes,
as explained in Tanya,
that through the matter of Daas one comes to love and its branches, and fear and its branches,
that love is the root of all 248 positive commandments,
and fear is the root of all 365 negative commandments.
